title: Deployment marshalling & quiet windows lab notes
content:
Context and quick brief:
- Purpose: scribble lab notes for 'marshalling' a deployment into a quiet window where client traffic is carefully funneled, warmed, and validated before opening the floodgates. Personal working doc — not the canonical runbook.
- When to use: complex model flips, cross-region traffic switches, or large capacity reshuffles where sudden traffic changes historically cause cache coldness / p95 spikes.
- Owner: Fiona (me). Collaborators: Marco (telemetry), Devon (infra ops), Sofia (sre on-call).

Goals for this experiment:
1) Validate small cohorts with shadowed KV cache priming so first real requests don't go cold.
2) Keep global p95 < 350ms and error rate < 0.5% during entire window.
3) Have a fast, deterministic escape hatch (traffic siphon) that can be executed in <2 minutes.
4) Gather data to tune warmup TTL and cohort sizes for future ops.

Definitions I am using here (my shorthand):
- Marshalling: steps to corral inbound traffic into a small, known set of cohorts that we can warm and observe.
- Anteroom cohort: a small warmup cohort sitting behind regular auth that simulates live load and warms KV/cache.
- Quiet window: a designated low-concurrency timeframe (typically 20–40 minutes) where we perform heavy priming operations and low-variance checks.

Assumptions / pre-req checks (pre-window):
- PR 482 merged and deployed to canary nodes in us-west2; health checks green for 20m. (see linked PR)
- Canary model variant tagged and pinned in routing table: variant=v2b-marshall
- Observability: dashboards have rolling 1h, 15m, 5m panels for p50/p95/p99, err%, token throughput, kv-cache-hit, cpu/gpu util. Marco to confirm panels exist.
- On-call (SRE) notified and confirmed availability.
- Capacity: reserve +20% spare GPU headroom for warm cohorts (DEVON to confirm autoscaler override).

Quiet window schedule (template) — times are local TZ, pick a low-traffic day:
- T-60m: announce in slack:#deployments and #sre-oncall; start preflight checks.
- T-45m: run synthetic warmup script (dry-run) for 10m against canary in shadow mode. Verify no errors.
- T-30m: begin marshalling: attach router rules to funnel 1% of new users into anteroom cohort (cohort size target = ~200RPS).
- T-20m: run KV priming job (seed frequent cache prefixes) across cohort nodes (script: tools/warm_kv.py --keys-list sample-1k.txt).
- T-10m: validate telemetry: p95 < 350ms, err% < 0.5; kv-cache-hit >= 75% for the cohort. If any fail, rollback routing to stable and abort.
- T-0: bump cohort -> 5% if metrics stable for 10m; otherwise hold and extend quiet window.
- T+20m: if metrics stable at 5% for 15m, start gradual ramp (2x every 10m) with automated checks between steps.

Telemetry checks (quick queries / alerts to watch):
- Latency: SELECT percentile(duration_ms, 95) FROM http_requests WHERE model="v2b-marshall" AND cohort="anteroom" LAST 5m
- Error rate: errors_total / requests_total over 5m for same filter
- KV hit ratio: kv_hits / (kv_hits + kv_misses) on cohort nodes
- Degenerate outputs: monitor rerank/fallback rate + downstream eval webhook failures (Sofia to instrument)
- Cost proxy: token/sec per GPU (to catch runaway token churn)

Escape hatch options (ranked):
1) Siphon traffic to stable variant (v2a) via router flag — immediate and safe.
2) Pin all customers to dedicated stable pool (if tenant-aware) — slower but preserves isolation.
3) Scale down canary pool and divert regionally (if issue seems infra-related).

Fast playbook for triggering escape hatch: (1) call out in slack with header "ESCAPE HATCH"; (2) run routing CLI: rtr set-route model=v2b-marshall -> variant=v2a --force; (3) verify p95 and errors for 5m; (4) create incident in JIRA-RELEASE-312 and tag SRE. Aim to complete in <2 minutes. Test this flow next week.

Observations to collect during the lab (for follow-up):
- time-to-first-token vs warmed cohort (measure impact of priming)
- KV hit decay curve after traffic ramp (minutes to 50% hit ratio)
- tail latency behaviors when cohort moves from 1% -> 5% -> 20%
- any mismatch between simulated and real client patterns (headers, session affinity)

Things I need / TODO (open items):
- [ ] Marco: add kv-cache-hit panel to the canary dashboard (low-effort panel).
- [ ] Devon: confirm autoscaler override isn't blocked by infra policy and set spare headroom.
- [ ] Sofia: hook the regression-eval webhook into the cohort stream; add quick alert if eval failure rate > 0.2%.
- [ ] Me: run a dry-run of the siphon command and document exact CLI steps with telemetry checks.
- [ ] Run a tabletop with SRE and Dev on Thu 2025-04-17.

Open questions / risks (thinking out loud):
- How much pre-seeding is enough? storing 10k keys vs 100k keys has cost/latency tradeoffs — need empirical job.
- Tenant fairness: small tenants might get pinned to anteroom and see degraded experience during ramp; need per-tenant guardrail.
- Billing spike: warmup jobs can temporarily increase token/compute; allocate budget to cover 2x normal for 30m.
- Observability gaps: we rely on a downstream eval webhook that hasn't been exercised under load. Risky.

Quick notes for future formatting into runbook:
- Replace ad-hoc times with relative checks (hold X minutes between steps).
- Make escape hatch CLI snippet a sticky snippet in confluence.
- Add recovery checklist (who to call, who has permission to run siphon).

Personal retrospective prompts after a run (what I'll scribble):
- What threshold did we hit first? (latency / errors / cost?)
- How long did cache warming take to flatten?
- Any surprise single-tenant effects?
- Was the siphon quick enough? Any failures during change?

End notes: this doc is intentionally messy — my brain dump before converting to a proper runbook. If we iterate this into the runbook, I want a small 'anteroom' template we can reuse across model flips.

-- Fiona
